accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective complex algebraic variety, and let c be an integral cohomology class in H^{2p}(X, Z) of Hodge type (p,p) that survives all differentials d_r in the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence from cohomology to topological K-theory. Must every such class c be an integral linear combination of cohomology classes cl(Z) of algebraic cycles Z of codimension p on X?
accepted.context_brief: Integral Hodge classes and Atiyah–Hirzebruch differentials

evidence.quote: The latter hence is in the kernel of the successive differentials dr of the spectral sequence. No counterexample is known to the statement that integral (p, p) classes killed by all dr are integral linear combinations of classes cl(Z).

accepted.question_text: Among integral (p,p)-classes on a smooth projective complex algebraic variety that are known or conjectured to come from algebraic cycles, which classes should be effective in the strong sense of being the class cl(Z) of a single codimension-p algebraic cycle Z, rather than only a difference of such classes?

evidence.quote: One has no idea of which classes should be effective, that is, of the form cl(Z), rather than a difference of such.

accepted.question_text: For a smooth projective complex algebraic variety X and a fixed codimension p, let J^p(X) be the extension of the group of integral cohomology classes of type (p,p) by the intermediate Jacobian J^p(X)^0, and let A^p(X) be the subgroup of J^p(X) generated by codimension-p algebraic cycles on X. What subgroup of J^p(X) is A^p(X)?
accepted.context_brief: Algebraic cycles inside the intermediate Jacobian

evidence.quote: No conjecture is available to predict what subgroup of Jp(X) the group Ap(X) is.

accepted.question_text: Consider a smooth projective algebraic family f : X → S defined over the algebraic closure Q̄ of Q in C, and fix an integral cohomology class on a typical fiber X_0. Is there an algorithm that decides whether this class becomes of Hodge type (p,p) on some fiber somewhere over the parameter space S?
accepted.context_brief: Algorithmic detection of Hodge classes in families

evidence.quote: Let (Xs)s∈S be an algebraic family of projective non-singular algebraic varieties: the fibers of a projective and smooth map f : X → S. We assume it is defined over the algebraic closure Q̄ of Q in C. No algorithm is known to decide whether a given integral cohomology class of a typical fiber X0 is somewhere on S of type (p, p).

accepted.question_text: In the same setting of a smooth projective family f : X → S defined over Q̄, the Hodge conjecture predicts that the locus in S where a fixed integral cohomology class becomes of type (p,p) is a denumerable union of algebraic subvarieties. Must that Hodge locus in fact be defined over Q̄?
accepted.context_brief: Field of definition of the Hodge locus

evidence.quote: The Hodge conjecture implies that the locus where this happens is a denumerable union of algebraic subvarieties of S (known: see [4]), and is defined over Q̄ (unknown).

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension N, and let Δ ⊂ X × X be the diagonal. The Künneth decomposition of the cohomology class cl(Δ) gives components cl(Δ)_{a,b} in H^a(X) ⊗ H^b(X) for a + b = 2N, and each of these components is a Hodge class. Are these Künneth components of the diagonal algebraic cycles?

evidence.quote: The Hodge conjecture is not known even in the following nice examples. Example 1. For X of complex dimension N, the diagonal Δ of X × X is an algebraic cycle of codimension N. The Hodge decomposition being compatible with Künneth, the Künneth components cl(Δ)a,b ∈ H a(X) ⊗ H b(X) ⊂ H 2N (X × X) (a + b = 2N ) of cl(Δ) are Hodge classes.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension N, let η ∈ H^2(X, Z) be the class of a hyperplane section, and for p ≥ 0 let η^p : H^{N-p}(X, C) → H^{N+p}(X, C) be the hard Lefschetz isomorphism. If z ∈ H^{N-p}(X, C) ⊗ H^{N-p}(X, C) is the Hodge class that represents the inverse map (η^p)^{-1}, is the class z algebraic?
accepted.context_brief: Algebraicity of the inverse hard Lefschetz correspondence

evidence.quote: Example 2. If η ∈ H 2(X, Z) is the cohomology class of a hyperplane section of X, the iterated cup product ηp : H N − p(X, C) → H N +p(X, C) is an isomorphism (hard Lefschetz theorem, proved by Hodge. See [10, IV.6]). Let z ∈ H N − p(X, C) ⊗ H N − p(X, C) ⊂ H 2N − 2p(X × X) be the class such that the inverse isomorphism (ηp)− 1 is c ↦→pr1!(z ∪ pr∗2 c). The class z is Hodge.
The Hodge conjecture is not known even in the following nice examples.

accepted.question_text: Let A be an abelian variety over the algebraic closure F of a finite field F_q. Suppose A is lifted in two different ways to characteristic 0, giving complex abelian varieties A_1 and A_2 defined over Q̄, and choose Hodge classes z_1 on A_1 and z_2 on A_2 of complementary dimension. After interpreting z_1 and z_2 as ℓ-adic cohomology classes and reducing them over F, is their intersection number κ always a rational number?
accepted.context_brief: Rationality of intersections of reduced Hodge classes

evidence.quote: The following corollaries of the Hodge conjecture would be particularly interesting. Let A be an abelian variety over the algebraic closure F of a finite field Fq. Lift A in two different ways to characteristic 0, to complex abelian varieties A1 and A2 defined over Q̄. Pick Hodge classes z1 and z2 on A1 and A2, of complementary dimension.
Interpreting z1 and z2 as ℓ-adic cohomology classes, one can define the intersection number κ of the reduction of z1 and z2 over F. Is κ a rational number?

accepted.question_text: In the same finite-field lifting setup, fix a Hodge class z_1 on one characteristic-0 lift of an abelian variety A over the algebraic closure F of F_q, reduce z_1 over F, and pair it with the cohomology class of an algebraic cycle on A itself. Must the resulting intersection number always be a rational number?
accepted.context_brief: Rationality of intersections with algebraic cycles after reduction

evidence.quote: If z1 and z2 were cl(Z1) and cl(Z2), Z1 and Z2 could be chosen to be defined over Q̄ and κ would be the intersection number of the reductions of Z1 and Z2.
Same question for the intersection number of the reduction of z1 over F with the class of an algebraic cycle on A.
